headline: Generative models now design biomolecules under explicit multi-objective constraints
label: Generative Biomolecular Design Models
summary: Diffusion, reinforcement fine-tuning, and agentic loops now embed diversity, target-directed objectives, and physics validation into biomolecule generation.
synthesis: The dominant thread is generative design of biomolecules under explicit, multiple objectives rather than single-property optimization. Discrete diffusion recurs as the generator: TD3B conditions it on agonist or antagonist transition direction for GPCR allosteric binders, and MuseDrift targets a specified sequence identity. Other items wrap generators in optimization or agentic loops: SGRPO adds set-level diversity rewards during fine-tuning, CatIF-RL steers inverse folding toward higher predicted kcat, and ToolMol and the polymer workflow call RDKit or OpenMM/Packmol as tools. What is new is explicit encoding of objectives, diversity, and physics-based validation within the generative loop. Evidence is largely preprint-level; SmileyLlama is the one published item.
